title: Retrieval quiz: marketing (4.1 to 4.3) and one 6-mark question
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 36 (Pupil PDF: marketing retrieval quiz and one 6-mark analyse question.)
intro: Answer from memory, then mark with the mark scheme.

questions.q: Give one example of primary research.
questions.a: For example: a survey, interview, focus group or observation

questions.q: Give one example of secondary research.
questions.a: For example: government statistics, market reports, competitors' websites

questions.q: What is the difference between quantitative and qualitative data?
questions.a: Quantitative: numbers that can be measured; qualitative: opinions and reasons
Dividing a market into groups of customers with similar needs (e.g. by age, income, location)

questions.q: Name the four stages of the product life cycle.
In the Boston matrix, what is a product with high market share in a low-growth market?

questions.a: Setting a low price to win market share quickly, then raising it
Setting a high price when a new product launches, then lowering it
For example: advertising, sales promotion, social media, sponsorship

questions.q: Give one advantage of selling online (place).
questions.a: Reach more customers at lower cost than shops

questions.q: Analyse how a small halal bakery could use social media to increase sales. (6)
questions.a: Low-cost posts reach local customers and show new products, so awareness and footfall rise; reviews build trust; offers can be targeted to segments (e.g. Ramadan orders). But it takes time and poor reviews spread quickly. Level 3 (5-6): a balanced analysis with two developed chains of reasoning, both in context. Level 2 (3-4): developed reasoning, partly in context. Level 1 (1-2): points identified with little development.
